line.text: That is {name}, Chancellor: a manifesto red line, and the words are on the record. Nothing here will stop you, and the public will notice.
On these numbers a rule is missed, and the OBR will say so on 28 October. The Charter’s escape clause is for an emergency or a significant shock, judged by the OBR, not for a choice.
{name} was funded when you left Downing Street. Nothing in your Budget funds it now.
{name} is below what you promised the Prime Minister: the lever has come back from the target you agreed.
Every flagship you agreed with the Prime Minister is still funded. What remains is whether the rules and your headroom survive the October forecast.
Headroom is below the target you set yourself. Remember what it is: a forecast margin. The OBR’s typical five-year error on receipts alone is about £32bn, bigger than any target on that list.
You are inside your own target. It is still a forecast: the OBR’s typical error over five years is about £32bn, and October’s numbers will be the OBR’s, not ours.
